Fixed-income assets are offering attractive yields again:

10Y Note Yield is currently trading above 5.10%, its highest level since July 2007.

At the same time, 30Y Note Yield is up to 5.44%, its highest since June 2007.

Investment-grade credit now yields 5.7%, its highest level since April 2024, followed by high-yield credit at 7.5%, its highest since May 2025.

Furthermore, private credit offers yields of 8.3% while risk-free money market funds offer 3.6%.

This marks a remarkable shift from the previous decade, when near-zero interest rates made it difficult to generate meaningful income from traditional fixed-income assets.

Higher for longer is creating meaningful income opportunities.

The average US stock is struggling.

The ratio of the equal-weighted S&P 500 to the S&P 500 index is down to 1.11, its 3rd-lowest level since April 2003.

This ratio has declined for 5 consecutive weeks by a total of -5.5%.

Over this period, the equal-weighted S&P 500 has fallen -4.4% while the S&P 500 has increased by +0.8%.

This also puts the ratio on track for its 4th consecutive annual decline, the longest streak since 1999.

By comparison, this metric peaked at 1.60 in April 2015.

AI is carrying the entire stock market.

Oracle stock ran to $245 this year, then round-tripped back to $140.

To win the OpenAI deal, Oracle signed hell-or-high-water leases and now owes rent whether or not the power ever turns on. The banks that lent $18 billion to build one New Mexico site are already dumping the loans below 90 cents on the dollar, a paper loss near $1.8 billion, and S&P cut Oracle to a notch above junk.

The AI buildout is running on borrowed money, and Oracle is where the credit is cracking first. $ORCL

Since ChatGPT launched, employment is up for every age group except the youngest. Workers 22 to 25 are the only cohort whose jobs have fallen.

Mid-career workers are up about 10% over the same stretch. AI took the entry-level busy work that 22-year-olds used to learn on, and companies stopped hiring as many of them.

The bottom rung of the ladder is the first thing AI automated. The productivity shows up in earnings. The missing jobs show up in the new grads.

tweets.text:
Diesel just hit a record $6.53 a gallon, up 77% in a year.

Contract truck rates are back to $3.11 a mile, the highest since 2022, and a Shanghai-to-LA container runs $8,102. Almost everything you buy rides on that freight, so the cost lands in your cart.

This is a supply shock, not inflation. A war spiked diesel and the trucker pool got thinner. The Fed cannot print fuel or a driver, so this clears when supply returns. Higher rates do nothing to speed it up.

Portland spent hundreds of millions building subsidized housing. Now some market-rate apartments rent for less than the subsidized ones.

A single mom skipped the affordable-housing waitlist and rented a market-rate 3-bedroom for $1,600, below the $1,800 average for an income-restricted unit. 8.3% of the city's affordable apartments now sit empty, the most since 2000.

This is what central planning does to a housing market. The mayor says the system could be insolvent within 6 months.

The 10-year Treasury yield just hit 5.23%, the highest since 2007. The 5% level that capped it for years is now the floor under it.

Foreign buyers are backing away. This week's 5-year auction cleared at 5.03% with foreign and indirect bidders taking just 54% versus their usual 65%. Fewer buyers for a record pile of debt means higher yields, and that keeps the pressure on stocks and mortgages.
